sections.label: Societies Act registration amendments
sections.summary: The Societies Act governs society registration, and MHA proposes amendments to strengthen regulation and clarify registration requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Societies Act governs the registration of societies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: It ensures that groups that may be used for unlawful purposes, pose a threat to safety and security, or whose activities are contrary to our national interests, are not allowed to establish themselves in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To ensure that the Societies Act remains relevant and can continue to meet its intent, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has proposed a set of amendments to: (a) strengthen the regulation of societies to safeguard national interests and security; and (b) provide better clarity to the public on the registration requirements.

sections.label: Automatic Route Registrar powers
sections.summary: Clause 4 lets the Registrar make inquiries and reject Automatic Route applications likely used unlawfully or contrary to national security or interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill, therefore, amends section 4A of the Societies Act to: remove the obligation on the Registrar to register a society under the Automatic Route without making an inquiry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This will allow the Registrar to make inquiries of applications submitted via the Automatic Route; and empower the Registrar to reject an application submitted via the Automatic Route, if the Registrar is satisfied that the society, if registered: (a) is likely to be used for unlawful purposes or for purposes prejudicial to public peace, welfare or good order in Singapore; or (b) would be contrary to Singapore’s national security or interest.

sections.label: Grounds for refusing name changes
sections.summary: Clause 8 amends section 11 to include grounds on which the Registrar may refuse a change of name or constitution amendment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To provide clarity to societies, clause 8 of the Bill amends section 11 to include the grounds on which the Registrar may refuse to approve a change of name or an amendment of provisions in the societies’ constitution.

sections.label: Registrar declares unfit officers
sections.summary: Clause 10 amends section 12(1)(b) to allow the Registrar, instead of the Minister, to declare a person unfit to be a society officer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For ease of administration, clause 10 of the Bill amends section 12(1)(b) of the Societies Act to allow the Registrar, instead of the Minister, to declare a person as unfit to be an officer of a society.

sections.label: Increased fines for Societies Act offences
sections.summary: Fine quantum for all Societies Act offences is increased to keep up with inflation and maintain a deterrent effect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The last review of the penalties in the Societies Act was done in 2004, 19 years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We are increasing the fine quantum for all the offences in the Societies Act to keep up with inflation and to ensure that the fine quantum continues to have a deterrent effect.

sections.label: One-stop service for charity societies
sections.summary: A one-stop service will let societies that are also charities file annual submissions only once, with details worked out later.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To reduce the administrative burden on societies which are also charities, a one-stop service will be established which allows such societies to file their annual submissions only once.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The details of the one-stop service will be worked out with Charities Unit later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I start by highlighting Article 14 of the Constitution of the Republic of Singapore.

sections.label: Societies Act gate-keeping role
sections.summary: A 2004 statement describes the Societies Act as gate-keeping, with section 4 letting the Registrar refuse registration in enumerated circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Indeed, in 2004, when the Act was last amended, the hon Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs then, Assoc Prof Ho Peng Kee, stated as follows in this House and I quote, "The Societies Act plays a gate-keeping role in ensuring that groups which may be used for unlawful purposes, or pose a threat to public order, welfare or good order in Singapore, or which will be contrary to our national interests are not allowed to establish themselves in Singapore." The operative provision is section 4 of the Act which vests with the Registrar the power to refuse the registration of a specified society in enumerated circumstances.

sections.label: Registrar discretion replacing shall
sections.summary: Clause 3(a) of the Bill replaces "shall" with "may", giving the Registrar a discretion instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Section 4 of the Act sets out the premises upon which he can reject a society's application." Under clause 3(a) of the Bill, it is proposed that the Registrar is vested with a discretion instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The word "shall" is proposed to be replaced with "may".

sections.label: Reversing 2004 automatic registration
sections.summary: The Bill reverses some 2004 liberalisations and lets the Registrar reject Automatic Route applications, removing automatic registration in all but name.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the 2004 Societies (Amendment) Bill, the "automatic regime" required the Registrar of Societies to register these societies on the date the application is received without making further inquiries, as long as the payment of the prescribed fee and other formalities are met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill before us today reverses some of the liberalisations to the Societies Act in 2004.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill also allows the Registrar to reject an application submitted via the Automatic Route if the Registrar is satisfied that the society, if registered, is likely to be used for unlawful purposes or for purposes prejudicial to public peace, welfare or good order in Singapore or would be contrary to Singapore's national interests or security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This effectively removes the automatic registration process in all but name, as every registration, even for societies that are not specified in the Schedule, will, henceforth, be subject to additional scrutiny.

sections.label: Support for Societies Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill, saying non-specified societies applying via the Automatic Route face Registrar inquiries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Societies can be vulnerable to, and potentially engage in, unlawful activities or be subject to undue foreign influence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I support the proposed Societies (Amendment) Bill, aimed at strengthening safeguards against such threats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the amendment, non-specified societies that apply via the Automatic Route are subject to inquiries by the Registrar to ascertain if they, indeed, qualify for registration via the Automatic Route.

sections.label: Question on Ministerial appeals
sections.summary: The speaker asks MHA how many appeals the Minister has reviewed for scheduled and non-specified societies and on what grounds they are granted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On this issue, I would like to ask MHA how many appeals have been reviewed over the years by the Minister for both scheduled and non-specified societies, and on what grounds are the appeals granted by the Minister.

sections.label: Support despite clarifications
sections.summary: The speaker states that, notwithstanding clarifications raised, they support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my clarifications raised, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Entrenching public peace and order
sections.summary: The Bill entrenches the country's determination to maintain public peace, welfare and good order and protect national interest.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The first of this duality is that it firmly entrenches our determination as a country to maintain public peace, welfare and good order, and protect what is in our national interest.

sections.label: Latitude for societies to flourish
sections.summary: The Bill increases maximum punishments and fines and clarifies the Registrar's powers, yet provides latitude for societies to flourish and advocate issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The second of this duality, Mr Deputy Speaker, is that the Bill, notwithstanding the increase of maximum punishments and fines and clarifications on the powers of the Registrar of Societies, provides latitude for societies to flourish and for like-minded individuals to share their common perspectives and come together to advocate, to promote, to discuss and to deepen understanding of a wide set of issues and interests.

sections.label: Registry of Societies registration figures
sections.summary: A Registry of Societies search found about 4,420 of 8,321 registered societies registered from 2001, and about 798 existed pre-Independence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 1 October 2023, via a simple search online on the Registry of Societies, I found that more than half, about 4,420 out of a total of 8,321 societies currently registered, are relatively new and were registered only at the turn of the century from 1 January 2001 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, it is noteworthy that almost one in 10 registered societies today, or about 798 of them, had already existed pre-Independence more than 58 years ago.

sections.label: Members participating and supporting enforcement
sections.summary: Members have participated in national and international platforms, and the speaker supports tough enforcement while hoping Government recognises organisations' contributions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some members of these organisations have stepped forward and seized the opportunity to participate in national conversations, such as the National Youth Council and the National Council of Social Services, as well as in the international arena, such as the ASEAN Youth Fellowship.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can balance the need to be firm when enforcing the regulations through this Societies (Amendment) Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I fully support the use of tough and expeditious methods to prevent organisations from being corrupt and unlawful or from having divisive elements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, I also hope that the Government can recognise the tremendous legacy, history and contributions of organisations that have been working hard over the decades to do good for the people of Singapore.

sections.label: Support for protecting national security
sections.summary: The speaker concludes in firm support of the stance to protect national security and interests.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, to conclude, I am in firm support of our stance to protect fiercely our national security and interests.

sections.label: Strengthening societies regulatory framework
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens the regulatory framework, expands the regulator's power and provides clarity on registration and administration of societies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My hope is that the Ministry considers these factors with perspective and discernment where they apply.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill strengthens the regulatory framework, expands the power of the regulator and provides clarity on the registration and administration of societies.

sections.label: Registry must give rejection reasons
sections.summary: The amendments will require the Registry of Societies to give reasons for rejecting a society's application to change its rules, name and place of business.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While I acknowledge the potential benefits of this expansion, I do have some clarifications and suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that the proposed amendments will require the Registry of Societies to give reasons for rejecting a society’s application to change its rules, name and place of business.

sections.label: Whistle-blower protection programmes proposed
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry would consider explicit whistle-blower protection programmes for reporting suspicious activities without fear of retaliation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On that, may I check if the Ministry would consider introducing explicit whistle-blower protection programmes to inform members, volunteers and beneficiaries or the public to report suspicious activities without fear of retaliation?

sections.label: Free-access database for societies
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a free-access database giving the public more information on societies has been considered.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Has consideration been given to the development of a free-access database that can provide greater information to the public?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By providing a tool to search for information on societies, the public can make informed decisions and play a role in monitoring and reporting suspicious activities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe the amendments are a positive step, and regulations can help create a more just, ethical and inclusive society that benefits not only its members but the larger community.

sections.label: Registrar including constitution clauses
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether letting the Registrar include or exclude clauses in a society's constitution before registration may be seen as excessive Government intervention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, we must consider if allowing the Registrar to include or exclude specific clauses into a society's constitution before it is registered might be seen as excessive Government intervention in its internal workings.

sections.label: National security and political societies
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on whether matters contrary to Singapore's national security or interest encompass political societies or those with political affiliations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Moreover, when the Bill references matters "contrary to Singapore's national security or interest", I wish to clarify whether this encompasses political societies or those with political affiliations.

sections.label: Scrutinising transnational societies' bank accounts
sections.summary: The speaker says it is critical to scrutinise transnational societies whose principal bank accounts may be in known tax havens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, it is critical to scrutinise transnational societies whose principal bank accounts may be situated in territories or countries that are known for being tax havens, such as the Cayman Islands, Bahamas or the British Virgin Islands.

sections.label: One-stop annual reports for charities
sections.summary: The passage raises practical considerations about a proposal letting societies that are also charities submit annual reports through a one-stop service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As we explore the proposal allowing societies that are also registered charities to submit their annual reports through a "one-stop" service, it brings to mind practical considerations.

sections.label: Societies registered in past year
sections.summary: A search from October 2022 to 2023 found over 100 societies registered, serving sectors such as community, hobbyists, arts and sports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Based on a simple search in the past year between October 2022 and 2023, we have seen over 100 societies registered, serving various sectors, such as the community, hobbyists, arts and sports.

sections.label: Checks, balances and applicant communication
sections.summary: The passage supports the Bill's ethos and checks but urges communicating with applicants, noting an average of five applications rejected yearly over five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While it is, of course, critical for the system to have sufficient checks and balances and hold malicious actors accountable, and I agree with the overall ethos of the Bill, it is also important to communicate with potential applicants and ensure that their applications are not being pre-emptively concluded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand that in the last five years, an average of five applications were rejected yearly.

sections.label: Timeline for one-stop portal
sections.summary: The passage appreciates a one-stop portal for societies that are also charities and asks the Ministry whether there is a timeline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Further, I appreciate the implementation of a one-stop portal for societies, which are also charities, to submit their annual submissions in streamlining the process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry have a timeline, as many are looking forward to this one-stop portal?

sections.label: Registrar's power to direct amendments
sections.summary: Under section 11A(2) of the Societies Act, the Registrar can direct a non-specified society to amend its constitution to safeguard national interest or public order.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Currently, under section 11A(2) of the Societies Act, the Registrar already has powers to direct a non-specified society to amend its constitution, if it is in the Registrar’s opinion that the amendments are needed to safeguard national interest, or public peace, welfare or good order in Singapore.

sections.label: Statutory appeals to the Minister
sections.summary: Over the past three years, four statutory appeals were received by the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Over the past three years, we received four statutory appeals to the Minister.

sections.label: Automatic Route approved applications
sections.summary: No automatically approved applications were thought to warrant rejection, but three triggered concerns due to applicants' antecedents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Mr Giam asked if there were any applications that were approved via the Automatic Route that should not have been approved because they posed a threat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: There were no applications that were automatically approved that we thought should not have been approved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: However, we have come across three applications that were submitted via the Automatic Route that triggered some concerns, as the applicants had some antecedents.

sections.label: Appeal to Minister over refusal
sections.summary: Applicants refused approval for not inserting rules can appeal to the Minister within 30 days under section 4(4) of the Societies Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If the Registrar refuses to approve their application due to their refusal to insert the rules, then the applicants can also appeal to the Minister within 30 days under section 4(4) of the Societies Act.

sections.label: Rejected applications in five years
sections.summary: In the past five years, 53 applications were rejected, which is 3.7% of all applications received.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In the past five years, 53 applications were rejected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This is 3.7% of all applications received during this period.

sections.label: FICA and religious harmony amendments
sections.summary: FICA allows designating politically significant persons and countermeasures, while the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act was amended for foreign donations and leadership.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In particular, FICA, which was passed in Parliament in 2021, will allow the Government to designate an entity, such as a registered society, as a politically significant person.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If there is a higher risk of foreign interference, the Government can also issue stepped-up countermeasures to impose stricter safeguards, such as disallowing foreign political donations, and foreigners from holding leadership positions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On religious organisations, we amended the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act in 2019, to require religious groups to disclose foreign donations and affiliations and to be subject to local leadership requirements.

sections.label: Societies Act definition of society
sections.summary: A society includes any club, company, partnership or association of 10 or more persons, except groups governed by other Acts, so virtual groups meet the definition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In the Societies Act, a society includes any club, company, partnership or association of 10 or more persons, whatever its nature or object, except for groups that are already governed by other Acts, such as companies under the Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Hence, groups that form in virtual spaces meet the technical definition of a society.

sections.label: Public access to society information
sections.summary: Free public access to society information is not being contemplated due to database costs, and charges are imposed to recover extraction costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Razwana suggested that the public have free access to information on societies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We are not contemplating this at this time as there are costs involved in maintaining a database and, for extraction of information, we currently impose charges to recover costs.

sections.label: Registrar moving applications to Normal Route
sections.summary: The Registrar can move an application to the Normal Route if it belongs to the specified route, and may be empowered to ask questions when it is unclear.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the first point, indeed, if the application, technically, were to belong to the specified route, as in it is part of the list of the Schedule of Specified societies, the Registrar can move the application to the Normal Route.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But there could be instances where it is not clear that the application falls within that Schedule of societies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Therefore, we will need to empower the Registrar to be able to ask questions and be able to then move the application to the Normal Route, if necessary.

sections.label: Empowering Registrar to ask societies questions
sections.summary: The Registrar should be empowered to ask questions about societies' intentions so they are registered under the correct route, given foreign interference risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For instance, as many Members have cited, we have seen geopolitical tensions; we have seen the possibility of foreign interference through various entities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We will have to make sure that we have the levers and that societies are not used for purposes that are prejudicial to good order, security, peace and harmony in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Therefore, we find it necessary, where there are questions as to the intentions of certain societies, to make available the levers and empower the Registrar to be able to ask questions to make sure that the societies are registered under the correct route.
